title: Let All the Heathen Writers Join
description: Let All the Heathen Writers Join in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 119, part 7, headed “Imperfection of nature, and perfection of scripture”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Let all the hea-then writ-ers join To form one per-fect book, Great God, if once com-par'd with thine, How mean their writ-ings look!

lines: Let all the heathen writers join
Great God, if once compar'd with thine,
Not the most perfect rules they gave
Nor lead a step beyond the grave;
I've seen an end of what we call
How short the powers of nature fall,
Yet men would fain be just with God
By works their hands have wrought;
In vain we boast perfection here,
And sinks our virtues down so far,
Our faith and love, and every grace,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
